correctness.rationale: For every integer \(d\ge3\) the full quadratic harmonic band splits under O(d-2) and coordinate swap into \(4+2+2(d-2)+(d-2)+d(d-3)/2\) dimensions. Exact spherical absolute moments give every full and wedge Gram entry. Three signed determinant identities at \(\lambda=1/4\) prove inertia and absence of additional plateau eigenvalues, while the scalar 4x4 trace and an explicit trial polynomial yield a simple scalar optimum above 3/4. Gamma log-convexity yields a vector-root crossing above 1/2. The other sectors are bounded by their positive traces. These arguments prove all ranges and the complete spectrum analytically; symbolic checker produced 9 verified identities and an independent full-monomial Gram checker matched \(3\le d\le12\) (515 counted checks). Computation is verification, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The perpendicular two-hemisphere wedge is a geometrically canonical partial-observation region with no rotational axis, and degree two is the first band containing a mixed uv mode that couples its two sign cuts. Exact spectral counts (\(d-1\) above \(1/2\), two strictly in the intermediate interval, \(d(d-3)/2\) exactly at \(1/4\)) quantify the observability structure over infinitely many sphere dimensions and are not available from the general matrix definition alone. The uniform fixed-size block solution and simple sharp maximizing line supply concrete all-dimensional spectral benchmarks. The result makes no unsupported higher-degree, noise, or publication-scale claim.
